items.stem: Which of the following statements about spherical mirrors is correct?
items.answer: A concave mirror forms a virtual image when the object is between F and P.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: "A concave mirror forms a virtual image when the object is between F and P." The other three are false.
options: f = 2R for a spherical mirror.
A concave mirror forms a virtual image when the object is between F and P.
A concave mirror always forms a real image.
A convex mirror can form a real image of a real object.

items.stem: Why are convex mirrors used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles?
items.answer: They always give an erect, diminished image and a wide field of view.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: Derive the relation f = R/2 for a spherical mirror of small aperture.
items.markingKey: Paraxial ray, angle of incidence θ (2); CF = FP for small θ (2); result (1).

items.stem: An object is placed 25 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Find the image position and magnification (use the Cartesian sign convention).
A convex rear-view mirror has a radius of curvature of 60 cm. An object is 60 cm in front of it. Find the image position and magnification.
items.markingKey: f = R/2 = +30 cm (1); 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/30 + 1/60 ⇒ v = +20.0 cm (behind the mirror) (1); m = −v/u = +0.333: virtual, erect, diminished (1).

items.stem: A concave mirror of focal length 24 cm forms an image that is virtual and 2 times the size of the object. Find the object distance.
items.markingKey: m = −v/u = 2 ⇒ v = −2u (1); 1/v + 1/u = 1/f (f = −24) ⇒ u = f(m − 1)/m (1) = −12.0 cm, i.e. 12.0 cm in front of the mirror (1).

items.stem: Find the focal length of a spherical mirror of radius of curvature 50 cm.
Does the focal length of a mirror depend on the medium in which it is placed? Explain.
items.answer: No; reflection does not depend on refractive index, so f = R/2 is unchanged.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm forms an image that is virtual and 3 times the size of the object. Find the object distance.
items.markingKey: m = −v/u = 3 ⇒ v = −3u (1); 1/v + 1/u = 1/f (f = −10) ⇒ u = f(m − 1)/m (1) = −6.67 cm, i.e. 6.67 cm in front of the mirror (1).

items.stem:

items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: magnified images form for objects within 2F; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

A is false, but R is true.

items.markingKey: (b) power of a lens: P = 1/f (f in metres), unit dioptre.
options: n₂/v − n₁/u = (n₂ − n₁)/R
P = 1/f (f in metres), unit dioptre
the angle of incidence in the denser medium for which the angle of refraction is 90°

items.stem: Find the critical angle for light going from a medium of refractive index 1.6 to air.
A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm forms an image that is virtual and 2 times the size of the object. Find the object distance.
items.markingKey: m = −v/u = 2 ⇒ v = −2u (1); 1/v + 1/u = 1/f (f = −10) ⇒ u = f(m − 1)/m (1) = −5.00 cm, i.e. 5.00 cm in front of the mirror (1).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about refraction and lenses is NOT correct?
items.answer: Apparent depth is greater than real depth for a pond viewed from above.
items.markingKey: (a) "Apparent depth is greater than real depth for a pond viewed from above." is false; the other three are true.
options: Apparent depth is greater than real depth for a pond viewed from above.
The power of a convex lens is positive.
Total internal reflection needs light to travel from a denser to a rarer medium.
Optical fibres work on total internal reflection.

items.stem: Find the deviation produced by a thin prism of angle 6° and refractive index 1.5.
An astronomical telescope has an objective of focal length 1500 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 4 cm. Find its magnifying power and length in normal adjustment.
A point object in air is 20 cm from the convex spherical surface (radius of curvature 20 cm) of a long glass rod of refractive index 1.33. Find the position of the image.
items.markingKey: n₂/v − n₁/u = (n₂ − n₁)/R (2) ⇒ 1.33/v = 0.33/20 + 1/(−20) (1) ⇒ v = −39.7 cm (2) (virtual, on the object side).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about refraction through a prism is NOT correct?
items.markingKey: (a) "At minimum deviation, i ≠ e." is false; the other three are true.
options: At minimum deviation, i ≠ e.
Deviation by a thin prism is δ = (n − 1)A.
Violet light deviates more than red light in a glass prism.
At minimum deviation the ray inside the prism is parallel to the base (for an isosceles prism).
